title: Paramartha Guru Tale 64
summary: A wandering charlatan alchemist visited the ashram, demonstrating a trick: by dropping a shiny silver rupee into a lump of fresh cow dung...
full_text:
A wandering charlatan alchemist visited the ashram, demonstrating a trick: by dropping a shiny silver rupee into a lump of fresh cow dung and muttering strange syllables, he retrieved two shiny coins (having concealed the second coin in his palm).

He whispered to Guru Paramartha: 'Master, the dung of your sacred white cow Kamadhenu possesses latent alchemical properties! If you bury silver coins in her manure piles for three days during the full moon, the dung will gestate and double the silver!'

The alchemist departed, leaving the seed of greed planted in the Guru's mind.

Guru Paramartha called Matti: 'Matti, our ashram emergency fund contains twenty silver rupees! Collect twenty fresh piles of cow dung from Kamadhenu, insert one silver coin into the center of each pile, and guard the mounds for three days!'

Matti collected twenty fresh, steaming piles of cow dung, arranged them in neat rows in the backyard, and pressed a shiny silver coin into the heart of each heap.

The five disciples stood guard day and night with sticks, chasing away crows and chickens.

On the third morning, the Guru and his disciples assembled to harvest their doubled fortune.

'Dig into the alchemical mounds!' commanded the Guru. 'We should find forty silver rupees!'

The disciples plunged their bare hands into the dried, crusty manure piles, searching through the dung with eager fingers.

They searched the first pile: empty!
They searched the second pile: empty!
They searched all twenty piles, coating their arms, fingers, and clothes in filthy manure: not a single silver coin was found in any pile!

Matti wailed: 'The silver has vanished! Where are our forty coins?'

Madayan examined the trampled ground and discovered footprints leading from the garden fence: 'Master! A tragedy of reverse alchemy! The manure piles did not double the silver; they dissolved the silver into ethereal vapor!'

At that moment, the village sweepers passed the fence, jingling twenty silver coins in their pockets, laughing merrily. They had watched Matti bury the coins three nights earlier and had dug them up thirty minutes after the disciples fell asleep!

The Guru stood amidst the trampled manure piles, his hands filthy, his robes soiled, and his treasury empty.

Guru Paramartha delivered his philosophical conclusion: 'We have proved through empirical research that cow dung is exceptionally fertile for vegetables, but completely infertile for silver!'

The disciples spent the afternoon at the river with five bars of soap, scrubbing the alchemical failure from their hands.
moral: Searching for gold in manure piles leaves you with dirty hands and empty pockets.
